core_obligations: Duality setup (proof lines 1331-1341): dim H^1(X, omega_X) = 1 and omega_X represents the H^1-dual functor on coherent modules.

Splitting argument (proof lines 1341-1353): given omega_X -> F -> Q -> 0 with H^1(X, Q) = 0, if H^1(X, F) is nonzero then the connecting map H^1(X, omega_X) -> H^1(X, F) is an isomorphism; by the universal property there is a map F -> omega_X whose action on H^1 is the inverse, and the universal property again shows the composition omega_X -> F -> omega_X is the identity, so F = omega_X (+) Q.
proof_roadmap: Fix the one-dimensionality of H^1(omega) and the representability of the dual functor.
Assume H^1(F) nonzero and deduce the isomorphism on H^1 from the vanishing on Q.
Construct the retraction F -> omega_X via the universal property.
Verify the composition is the identity and conclude the splitting.
difficulty_reason: The lemma dichotomizes extensions of the dualizing sheaf: either the cohomology of F vanishes or the sequence splits (statement lines 1321-1329). The proof (lines 1331-1353) is a complete representability argument: the one-dimensionality of H^1(omega), the isomorphism induced on H^1, the retraction constructed through the universal property, and the identity check closing the splitting. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a compact duality argument with one universal property used twice, correctly ordered.
